questions.question: What happens if a trailer is not at the proper height during coupling?

options.text: It will not make a difference.
Coupling will be more secure.
It may not couple correctly.

questions.explanation: Before coupling a tractor and trailer, check that the trailer is at the correct height. If it is too low, the trailer nose may be damaged. If it is too high, it may not couple correctly.

questions.question: While driving, what should a driver pay attention to?

options.text: Not worry about what is happening on the sides of the vehicle.
Pay attention to what is happening on all sides of the vehicle.
Not worry about what is happening behind the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pay attention to what is happening on all sides of the vehicle.
questions.explanation: You must be aware of what is happening on all sides of your vehicle at all times. Look ahead at the road and check both side mirrors regularly while driving.

questions.question: What should you do if your vehicle gets stuck on railroad tracks?

options.text: Stay in the vehicle.
Get out of the vehicle and call for help.
Keep trying to get your vehicle off the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get out of the vehicle and call for help.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle gets stuck on railroad tracks, leave immediately and move away from the tracks. Look for emergency contact information on the signposts or signal boxes at the crossing. Call 911 or another emergency number right away.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a type of distraction?

options.text: Physical
Mental
Obtuse

questions.explanation: Distractions fall into three types: physical (like reaching for an object), mental (like talking with a passenger), or both (like using a hand-held phone).

questions.question: What should you do after finishing a pre-trip inspection?

options.text: Leave the rear shut-off valves open.
Remove the service line valve.
Close the emergency line valve.

questions.explanation: Before driving, open the rear emergency line and service line shut-off valves to check that air reaches all brake lines. You should hear air escaping. Close both valves before you start driving.

questions.question: Why is rolling backward when starting to accelerate dangerous?

options.text: The transmission may be damaged.
The truck is not made to go backwards.
You may hit a vehicle behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may hit a vehicle behind you.
questions.explanation: Make sure you can accelerate without rolling back first. Rolling backwards can cause you to hit a vehicle or object behind your truck.

questions.question: How do you test the tractor protection valve?

options.text: Remove the air supply knob.
Remove the parking brake control knob.
Release air with the brake pedal.
Release air with the gas pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release air with the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: To test the tractor protection valve, let the air supply charge fully. Turn off the engine. Then release air from the system by pressing the brake pedal several times. The valve should move to its emergency position when pressure drops to an unsafe level.

questions.question: In cold weather, what happens as the temperature rises and ice begins to melt?

options.text: It is usually safe to drive.
The road becomes even more slippery.
Traction increases.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road becomes even more slippery.
questions.explanation: As temperature rises and ice melts, the road surface becomes even more slippery. Water from melting sits on top of the ice and reduces traction further. Slow down and drive carefully on slippery roads.

questions.question: What should happen when you start an engine?

options.text: The brakes will lock up.
Warning lights should come on, then turn off quickly.
Coolant temperature should decrease.

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning lights should come on, then turn off quickly.
questions.explanation: After starting the engine, warning lights and buzzers should turn off after a few seconds. If they stay on, something may be wrong with the vehicle.

questions.question: What might rust around wheel nuts mean?

options.text: It rained recently.
The nuts are loose.
The nuts are too tight.

questions.explanation: Inspect your tires before every trip. Rust around wheel nuts may show that they are loose.

questions.question: You are braking on dry pavement at 55 mph. How much distance does brake lag add to your total stopping distance?

options.text: 32 feet
45 feet
20 feet

questions.explanation: Total stopping distance has four parts: perception distance, reaction distance, brake lag distance, and braking distance. At 55 mph on dry pavement, brake lag adds about 32 feet to your total stopping distance.

questions.question: You see an aggressive driver involved in a crash ahead. What should you do?

options.text: Stop and confront the driver.
Stop at a safe distance from the crash, wait for police, and tell them about the driver's aggressive behavior.
Block the driver in with your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop at a safe distance from the crash, wait for police, and tell them about the driver's aggressive behavior.
questions.explanation: Stop at a safe distance from the crash scene. Wait for police to arrive and tell them about the aggressive behavior you saw.

questions.question: When you visually check a coupling device, what should you look for?

options.text: Look for mud on the fifth wheel.
Make sure the kingpin is polished.
Make sure there is a space between the upper and lower fifth wheel.
Make sure the locking jaws are closed on the kingpin.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure the locking jaws are closed on the kingpin.
questions.explanation: Check that the locking jaws are securely closed around the kingpin. There should be no space between the upper and lower fifth wheel.

questions.question: Why are ice cream trucks a hazard to other drivers?

options.text: Ice cream trucks must be kept cold.
Children often run toward an ice cream truck without looking for traffic.
Ice cream trucks leave trails of water and ice on the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Children often run toward an ice cream truck without looking for traffic.
questions.explanation: Ice cream trucks attract children. Children may run to them without paying attention to other vehicles on the road.

questions.question: Where are regrooved tires allowed on a bus?

options.text: Allowed only on the front of a bus.
Allowed only on the rear of a bus.
Not allowed anywhere on a bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allowed only on the rear of a bus.
questions.explanation: Regrooved, recapped, or retreaded tires cannot be used on the front of a bus. They are only allowed on the rear.
